title: What's Buried in Division 1: Hidden Requirements That Blow Up Subcontract Scopes
summary: Division 1 buries requirements that kill subcontract margins. Learn which clauses estimators miss most — and what they cost downstream.
body_text: TL;DR Division 1 is the most-missed spec section in pre-construction — and one of the most expensive to ignore. Requirements buried in General Requirements (Sections 01 10 00 through 01 78 00) routinely transfer cost risk from owners and designers to GCs and subs. Specific examples: $300K in lead-lined glass absorbed under "readily inferable" language, $400K in missed roof cover board, $10K in destroyed material with no protection clause. The anti-patterns that create these gaps are predictable — and fixable before bid day. Provision's Chat Agent and Scope Agent help estimating teams surface Division 1 requirements across full project sets in under 60 minutes. Every estimator knows to read the drawings. Most read the trade specs. Fewer read Division 1 — at least not carefully. That's where the money gets lost. Division 1 — MasterFormat's General Requirements — is where owners and their lawyers embed the obligations that don't belong anywhere else. Coordination requirements. Submittal schedules. Testing protocols. Temporary facilities. Commissioning obligations. Administrative procedures that cost real money to execute. None of it shows up on a drawing. Most of it gets missed at buyout. All of it becomes a dispute. According to the Arcadis 2025 Global Construction Disputes Report , "errors and omissions in contract documents" has been the number one dispute cause for six of the last nine years. The average U.S. construction dispute now costs $60.1 million. Division 1 isn't the only driver — but it's a consistent contributor that most pre-construction teams underestimate. Why Division 1 Gets Skipped It's a volume problem. On a major institutional project, Division 1 alone can run 80 to 150 pages. It reads like legal language crossed with administrative policy. There are no details to circle, no dimensions to check — just dense prose with cost buried in every paragraph. Estimators under bid-day pressure make a rational trade-off: spend time where the dollars are most visible. Trade specs. Drawings. Schedules of values. Division 1 gets a skim — or gets handed to someone junior. That trade-off costs margin downstream. A Pre-Construction Lead at a Top-ENR Canadian GC put it plainly: "If you miss anything, they'll bill it." And increasingly, they're right to. Subcontractors in 2026 are more contract-sophisticated than they were five years ago. The informal "gentleman's agreement" is fading. As one Estimating Manager at a Canadian ICI GC noted: "We have less subs who just kind of a gentleman's agreement… they've become more quick to clarify that we're not including that one piece of scope." When a sub's scope letter excludes what Division 1 says is included, someone pays. Usually the GC. The Sections Most Likely to Bite You Not all of Division 1 carries equal risk. These sections generate the most downstream disputes — and get the least attention during bid review. 01 14 00 — Work Restrictions This section sets limits on hours, access, sequencing, and noise. It sounds administrative. It isn't. Restricted access windows on occupied hospital projects or phased school renovations can add 20–40% to a trade's labor cost. If the restriction isn't in the sub's scope, the GC owns the gap. 01 25 00 — Substitution Procedures Substitution windows are typically defined here — often 30 to 60 days post-award. Miss that window and subs lose the right to propose alternates. That affects buyout strategy and value engineering timelines. Most estimators don't calendar these dates at bid time. 01 31 00 — Project Management and Coordination This section governs who attends coordination meetings, how often, and in what format. On complex MEP-intensive projects, BIM coordination requirements alone — level of detail, clash detection, submission cadence — can represent significant unbilled labor for trade foremen and project engineers. Subs rarely price coordination overhead explicitly. GCs rarely check whether their scope sheets capture it. 01 33 00 — Submittal Procedures Submittal requirements in Division 1 specify format, number of copies, review turnaround expectations, and resubmittal limits. On federal or institutional work, requirements can be unusually stringent. If a sub's scope doesn't address submittals explicitly, and the spec requires electronic BIM submittals in a specific format, that's a cost gap — and a schedule risk. 01 40 00 — Quality Requirements Testing and inspection requirements live here. Special inspections, geotechnical verification, mock-up requirements, third-party QA. The question of who pays for failed tests — and re-tests — is frequently ambiguous in subcontract scopes. Division 1 often answers it. Subcontract scopes rarely reference it. A curtainwall mock-up, for example, can cost $80,000 to $150,000 to build and test. If the scope sheet says "per plans and specs" without explicitly naming this requirement, the sub will clarify it at buyout — or dispute it at construction. 01 50 00 — Temporary Facilities and Controls Temporary heat, hoarding, scaffolding, access roads, site trailers, security, fencing. Division 1 defines what's required. Scope sheets should define who provides it. When neither document is specific, the finger-pointing starts. A $10,000 glulam beam destroyed in a lay-down yard because no clause required material protection on site — that example from our Scope Gap Playbook illustrates the kind of cost that seems small but compounds across a project. Multiply it across twenty trades on a complex institutional project, and the math is painful. 01 73 00 — Execution Field conditions, existing utilities, cutting and patching, coordination with other trades. This section often contains language requiring contractors to "verify existing conditions before commencing work." That sounds reasonable. In practice, it transfers responsibility for unforeseen conditions to whoever signed the contract without a specific carve-out. 01 77 00 / 01 78 00 — Closeout Requirements O&M manuals. As-built drawings. Training requirements. Commissioning participation. Warranty documentation. These requirements frequently expand between design development and issued-for-construction. Scopes written at bid time rarely get updated to reflect them. Closeout drags — and so does final billing — when these aren't scoped explicitly. The Anti-Patterns That Create Division 1 Gaps The Scope Gap Playbook identifies eight habits that separate high-margin pre-construction teams from the rest. Division 1 exposure tends to cluster around a specific set of anti-patterns. "As per plans and specs." The most-cited anti-pattern in 200+ GC interviews. When a scope sheet says "as per plans and specs" and stops there, it incorporates Division 1 by reference — but without confirming that anyone read it. The sub reads it their way. The GC reads it theirs. The owner reads it a third way. Disputes follow. Copy-paste from the previous similar job. Division 1 requirements vary by owner, architect, and jurisdiction. A hospital project's Division 1 looks nothing like a commercial office building's. Scopes recycled from a prior project carry the prior project's assumptions. Those assumptions break when the new spec says something different. Junior estimators stuffing previous scopes verbatim. When bandwidth is tight, Division 1 review gets delegated down. Junior estimators may not know what to look for. They copy the format that worked last time. That's how $300,000 in lead-lined glass for a hospital imaging suite disappears from a scope sheet — absorbed by the GC under "readily inferable" language that no one caught at bid. That example comes directly from operator interviews in the Scope Gap Playbook . It's not hypothetical. The five-minutes-before-bid review. Scope review happens too late to course-correct. By the time someone spots the mock-up requirement or the BIM coordination protocol buried in Section 01 31 00, the sub's number is locked and the GC's bid is going in. The fix happens post-award — if it happens at all. What Division 1 Review Actually Requires Thorough Division 1 review isn't about reading every word. It's about knowing what to look for and where to find it — fast. That means building a checklist tied to the specific sections that carry cost risk. It means cross-referencing Division 1 obligations against each subcontract scope before buyout. And it means doing that review early enough in the bid cycle to adjust scopes, ask questions, or issue RFIs — not at 4:00 PM on bid day. A Director of Pre-Construction at a Mid-Market Southeast GC described the handoff problem well: "Pre-con is working in the scope sheet world and project management is working in the scopes of work." Division 1 gaps are born in that gap — written during bid, invisible during construction, expensive at closeout. What a Division 1 Checklist Should Cover Work restrictions and access limitations (Section 01 14 00) Substitution windows and approval timelines (Section 01 25 00) BIM coordination requirements and meeting obligations (Section 01 31 00) Submittal format, quantity, and resubmittal rules (Section 01 33 00) Special inspections and mock-up requirements (Section 01 40 00) Temporary facilities responsibility matrix (Section 01 50 00) Cutting, patching, and existing conditions language (Section 01 73 00) Closeout deliverables: O&M manuals, as-builts, training, commissioning (Section 01 77–78 00) Liquidated damages triggers and notice requirements Schedule of values format and billing requirements This list isn't exhaustive. Every project set is different. The point is that Division 1 review needs structure — not a skim. How Technology Helps — and Where It Falls Short General-purpose AI tools — ChatGPT, Copilot — can read text. They can't read a full project set and tell you that Section 01 40 00 requires a curtainwall mock-up that isn't referenced in any of the twenty-three subcontract scopes you're building for this pursuit. Provision's Chat Agent is purpose-built for this problem. It ingests the full project set — drawings, specs, contracts, addenda — and answers specific questions with cited references. Ask "What are the BIM coordination requirements in this spec?" and you get an answer tied to the exact clause, in under 20 seconds. Provision has processed over 66,000 construction documents and answered more than 50,000 queries across real project sets. That's what allows construction-specific AI to return accurate, citation-backed answers — not summaries that sound plausible but miss the clause that matters. For scope package generation, Scope Agent reads the full project set and builds complete scope-of-work packages in under 60 minutes. That includes pulling Division 1 obligations into trade-specific scopes — so the coordination meeting requirement in Section 01 31 00 shows up in the mechanical scope, not just in the spec no one re-read after bid day. Teams using Provision report an 80% reduction in document review time. For firms handling multiple pursuits simultaneously — and with the institutional pipeline up 22% year-over-year in 2026, many are — that's the difference between a thorough review and a skim. You can also explore the scope of work template Provision has built for GC teams — it includes Division 1 cross-reference fields that most standard templates skip. Tying It to the Subcontract Finding Division 1 requirements is step one. Making sure they appear in subcontract scopes is step two. That's where most teams fall short. The Eight Habits from the Scope Gap Playbook are clear on this: use specific document references, not generic incorporation. A scope sheet that says "contractor shall comply with Section 01 40 00" is more defensible than one that says "as per specs." More importantly, it's more useful — the sub knows what's expected, the GC has a reference point for disputes, and project management has a clear handoff document. The Pre-Construction Lead who gave us the "peanut-butter test" said it directly: "It's descriptive — bread, put it on a plate, use the open jar… You have to get to that level of detail or else they'll just be like, 'you didn't tell us that.'" That standard applies to Division 1 requirements as much as anything else in a subcontract scope. General language doesn't protect anyone. Specific language does. For a deeper look at subcontract language and scope gap prevention — including the "readily inferable" clauses that create the most risk — see the subcontract language chapter of the Scope Gap Playbook . The Cost of Not Reading Division 1 The FMI Construction Disconnected report puts annual U.S. rework costs from miscommunication and bad project data at $31 billion. Twenty-six percent is attributed to communication breakdowns. Twenty-two percent to bad project data. Division 1 gaps feed both categories. On projects where scope packages are weak and Division 1 is treated as background reading, change orders as a share of project cost routinely exceed 8–14% — and climb above 25% when scope definition is poor at bid (Navigant, republished by AIA). The firms with the best margins don't have better luck. They do the pre-bid work that makes Division 1 visible, specific, and binding before the subcontract is signed. If your estimating team is handling more complex institutional projects in 2026, the exposure only grows. The time to build Division 1 review into your standard process is before the next bid — not after the next dispute. See how the EllisDon team used Provision to identify over $1.8M in risk on a single project. Or review the full Provision platform for general contractors to understand how Scope Agent and Chat Agent work together in a real bid workflow. Frequently Asked Questions What is Division 1 in construction specifications? Division 1 — General Requirements — is the MasterFormat section covering administrative, procedural, and temporary requirements that apply to all trades on a project. It includes submittal procedures, quality requirements, coordination obligations, temporary facilities, and closeout deliverables. It applies to every subcontract, which is why missed requirements here affect the entire project. Why do estimators miss Division 1 requirements during bidding? Division 1 runs 80–150 pages on complex projects and reads like policy, not technical specifications. Under bid-day time pressure, estimators prioritize trade specs and drawings where cost is more visible. Division 1 gets skimmed or reviewed by junior staff — which is where most gaps originate. What are the most expensive Division 1 clauses to miss? Mock-up requirements (Section 01 40 00), BIM coordination obligations (Section 01 31 00), temporary facilities responsibility (Section 01 50 00), and closeout deliverables (Sections 01 77–78 00) are the highest-cost missed items. Individually, they range from tens of thousands to over $100,000. Across a project, they compound quickly. How do Division 1 gaps affect subcontract buyout? When Division 1 requirements aren't reflected in scope sheets, subs exclude them during buyout — either explicitly or by omission. The GC is then left covering the gap, negotiating a change after award, or accepting the risk. Subs in 2026 are more contract-literate than in prior years, which means informal assumptions get formalized as exclusions faster. How can AI help with Division 1 spec review? Purpose-built construction AI like Provision's Chat Agent ingests the full project set and answers specific Division 1 questions with cited clause references in under 20 seconds. Scope Agent pulls Division 1 obligations into trade-specific scope packages — so coordination and submittal requirements flow into subcontract scopes automatically, not as an afterthought at buyout. What's the difference between reading Division 1 and acting on it? Reading Division 1 means identifying the requirements. Acting on it means ensuring those requirements appear — explicitly, by section reference — in every affected subcontract scope before buyout. Most teams do the first inconsistently. Very few do the second systematically. That's where scope gaps become change orders. Where can I learn more about scope gap prevention in subcontract scopes? The Scope Gap Playbook is built from 200+ GC interviews and covers the habits, anti-patterns, and trade-specific gaps that drive cost overruns from bid through closeout. title: Dear Passengers Multiplayer: How Co-op Works + a Free Multiplayer Plane Game
summary: How Dear Passengers co-op works - pilot and cabin crew roles, physics chaos - plus a free multiplayer plane crash game you can play in your browser today.
body_text: Nobody is wishlisting Dear Passengers to play it alone. The entire pitch is co-op: you and your friends are the crew of the world's worst airline, and the game is what happens when everything goes wrong at once. Here's everything known about how Dear Passengers multiplayer works - and a free multiplayer plane crash game you can play in your browser right now. How Dear Passengers co-op works Dear Passengers, from developer FLEXUS, splits the crew across roles: One player takes the cockpit and actually flies the plane through weather, turbulence, and air pockets. Everyone else works the cabin: serving meals, calming passengers, securing cargo, and fixing whatever breaks next. Before takeoff, the crew picks which passengers and cargo to accept - riskier choices pay more, and some crates contain things like live crocodiles. Everything is physics-driven, and the plane pitches under your feet, so even walking down the aisle is a challenge mid-crisis. It's the Overcooked formula strapped to a failing aircraft: divided attention, constant small emergencies, and success depending entirely on how well your group communicates while screaming. The catch: you can't play it yet Dear Passengers is targeting a 2026 release on Steam. There's no demo and no early access - just a wishlist button. Player count hasn't been officially confirmed either. Play a free multiplayer plane crash game right now ATTENTION PASSENGERS is a free browser game inspired by Dear Passengers, and it has a multiplayer mode with a twist: instead of cooperating, you're competing. Everyone is on the same doomed plane, disasters keep hitting, and the goal is to survive longer than the other players - with sabotage very much allowed. Shove debris toward rivals, grab passengers, and be the last one standing when the wreck settles. Play ATTENTION PASSENGERS multiplayer free - browser-based, no download, with a single-player survival mode too if your friends are offline. Fair warning from the developer: multiplayer physics is the hardest thing in this genre to get right, and the multiplayer mode is rougher around the edges than single-player. That's part of the charm - half the fun is the jank. Frequently asked questions Is Dear Passengers online co-op? Yes, it's built around online co-op multiplayer, with one player flying and the others managing the cabin. How many players does Dear Passengers support? An exact count hasn't been confirmed. The structure - one pilot plus a cabin crew - suggests small groups, similar to other co-op chaos games. Does Dear Passengers have a release date? It's targeting 2026 on Steam. title: Ferrari Challenge Trofeo Pirelli UK Announces 2027 Calendar
body_text: Brands Hatch, 26 July 2026 – The 2027 Ferrari Challenge Trofeo Pirelli UK calendar was unveiled during the fifth round of the 2026 season at Brands Hatch. The ninth edition of the regional series will feature five rounds across the United Kingdom and the Netherlands, reaffirming a schedule that combines some of the most historic and prestigious circuits in British motorsport. The season will get underway at Silverstone from 23 to 25 April, with the iconic British venue hosting the opening round of the 2027 campaign. The second event will take place at Zandvoort, in the Netherlands, from 28 to 30 May, continuing the tradition of Ferrari Challenge UK visiting a circuit beyond British shores, before returning to the UK for the third round at Snetterton on 26 and 27 June, a demanding and highly technical circuit that has long been regarded as one of the toughest challenges on the calendar. From 23 to 25 July, the championship will move to Donington Park for a joint event with the Ferrari Challenge Trofeo Pirelli Europe, bringing together the two one-make series of the Prancing Horse on one of Britain's most historic circuits for one of the highlights of the season. The campaign will conclude at Brands Hatch from 3 to 5 September, where the 2027 season will come to a close and the class titles will be decided. 2027 Ferrari Challenge Trofeo Pirelli UK Calendar 23–25 April – Silverstone 28–30 May – Zandvoort 26–27 June – Snetterton 23–25 July – Donington Park 3–5 September – Brands Hatch 26 luglio 2026

How will you renovate your swimming pool?
summary: When it comes to renovating your pool, there are many possibilities. Follow our advice on how to go about it!
body_text: Renovating your swimming pool becomes more and more essential over time. But apart from the liner, which you have to renew regardless after a certain number of years, the possibilities are many. Not sure where to start? Here are our recommendations for the best actions you can take when it's time to renovate your pool and replace its equipment! Renovate to benefit from a more economical pool with better quality water Installing a variable speed pump is one of the best improvements that a pool can enjoy. A pump of this kind rotates water 24h/24 at a low speed: it therefore consumes little energy (up to 70% less than a single speed pump !), enables continuous water filtration and does all this very quietly. Replacing your sand filter with an element filter (with cartridges) is another way of saving money and improving the water filtration quality . A 4-cartridge filter filters the water very finely, which therefore requires less maintenance (treatment products), and can only be rinsed once at the end of the season: much less water (and time) wasted than with the frequent backwashing that comes with a sand filter! Renovate to make pool maintenance easier Imagine no longer needing to check the water quality of your pool, no longer having to control the pump speed yourself, or not even having to monitor the water level in the pool! All of this is possible, e.g. with an automatic water treatment system, which doesn't just inject salt or chlorine at set times, but analyses your water first so that it can then be treated with the right quantity of treatment products. And even more is possible with the installation of an automation system which helps your equipment communicate with itself: an incredibly efficient way of taking a large amount of pool maintenance work off your hands. PH level, quantity of chlorine or salt in the water, pump function, water level...automatically controlled, and can be monitored from your smartphone. Convenient, isn't it? Moreover, a system like this also helps you save money by using the right dose of treatment products at the right time, and only making your equipment function when it's really necessary. Renovate to swim in the pool for longer, in more comfort Making swimming season last longer, and enjoying water at a pleasant and gentle temperature all year round, is possible thanks to the heat pump . This installation is the most virtuous heating system , which creates more heat compared to the energy it uses. An economical way of swimming for as long as possible! But if you really want to do things as efficiently and virtuously as possible, install a cover on your pool first. Because open air water cools down, continuously evaporates and is exposed to UV rays from the sun which destroy the chlorine. A cover should therefore be considered first to have a more comfortable, economical and virtuous pool. Renovate your pool progressively, year by year You don't have to make all these changes at once. It's certainly useful to take advantage of renovating the pool when you need to replace the equipment, but you can also do it on a year-by-year basis to even out costs. It's your pool, so don't hesitate: the latest equipment will be much more convenient for you than older installations, consequently saving you money and making your swimming pool more virtuous than ever before.

title: Which Training Topics Need Animation vs Slide-Style Video?
summary: Choose the right training video format with a practical framework for animation, slide-style video, screenshots, demonstrations, and mixed formats.
body_text: The MOTION decision framework Score no points and invent no false precision. Instead, discuss these six questions with the subject expert and instructional designer. M, Movement Is actual movement, transformation, or timing part of what must be learned? If yes, favour animation, demonstration, or screen recording. If no, a stable visual may be sufficient. O, Observability Can the important event be filmed or captured accurately? Invisible or impossible mechanisms may need explanatory animation. Visible physical skills usually benefit from authentic demonstration. Interface detail usually benefits from real screens. T, Task fidelity How closely must training resemble the performance environment? High-fidelity needs push toward real equipment, interfaces, language, and constraints. Low-fidelity conceptual orientation can use simplified diagrams or animation. Never let style remove cues needed for transfer. I, Inspection Must learners compare, read, calculate, or examine a stable configuration? Use slide-style layouts, static diagrams, downloadable references, or learner-controlled frames. Fast motion makes inspection harder. O, Outcome and risk What happens if the learner misunderstands? Higher-risk topics demand stronger source control, expert review, accessibility checks, and often practice or assessment beyond video. Risk does not automatically determine visual style; it determines evidence and assurance. N, Navigation and maintenance Will learners need to find one fact later? Will the content change frequently? Choose modular scenes, transcripts, chapters, and companion text. A highly animated five-minute sequence may be expensive to update when one number changes. Stable components can be easier to replace, but actual maintainability depends on the tool and source files. Applied examples Fire-extinguisher selection Use slide-style comparison for extinguisher categories and decision criteria. Use demonstration for handling and safe stance. Animation can show consequences or simplified fire behaviour only when technically validated. A video alone should not substitute for required practical training. How a refrigeration cycle works Use animation for refrigerant movement and state changes, with a stable labelled system diagram as an anchor. Pause at meaningful phases. Let narration and highlighting correspond to the same component. Data-protection policy update Use a restrained slide-style structure: what changed, who is affected, required action, and escalation. Add a scenario for a borderline request. Link to the current policy and job aid. CRM opportunity entry Use authentic screen capture or simulation for exact fields and feedback. A slide-style introduction can explain the business rule. Re-record volatile interface scenes without regenerating the durable conceptual section. Difficult customer conversation Use a filmed or animated scenario to show choices, tone, and consequences. Follow it with stable decision prompts and reflection. If realism of facial expression is essential, test whether the chosen animation style carries enough nuance. Organisational induction Slide-style video can orient learners to structure, values, and resources. A presenter may add welcome and credibility. Avoid animated movement that contributes nothing to understanding. Mixed-format storyboarding Do not force an entire course into one visual mode. A storyboard might use a stable diagram for the whole model, animation for one changing process, a real screenshot to connect it to work, and a slide-style recap to stabilise the decision rule. Consistency comes from shared terminology, visual grammar, voice, brand, navigation, and accessibility, not from making every scene move the same way. Multimedia-learning research offers two cautions. First, words and pictures should be designed around how learners process information, not around the prestige of the delivery technology. Second, animation is not automatically superior to static graphics. Learner control, segmentation, signalling, prior knowledge, and the accuracy of the representation affect the result. Accessibility is part of format choice The visual format changes what must be made available in other modes. W3C’s WCAG 2.2 guidance says prerecorded audio in synchronised media requires captions at Level A, except for the stated media-alternative case. Captions include relevant non-speech audio and speaker identification, not only dialogue. At Level AA, important visual information not conveyed in the main soundtrack requires audio description. Plan this in the script: speak essential labels and state changes; do not communicate status by colour alone; give learners enough time to read; provide accurate captions and a useful transcript; avoid flashing and unnecessary motion; use player controls that support pause, replay, and navigation. Narrating the essential action can make a video more robust for many learners, but it does not automatically prove WCAG conformance. Test the finished media and player. For current product options, compare AI video tools for training and education and the best AI training video generators . FAQ Is animation more engaging than slides? Not inherently. Relevant motion can focus attention; decorative motion can distract. Evaluate comprehension and task performance, not assumed engagement. Are slide-style videos just narrated PowerPoints? They can be, but effective slide-style video is designed for asynchronous viewing with concise scenes, purposeful visuals, signalling, and suitable pacing. Can one training video mix animation and slides? Yes. A stable overview followed by an animated process and a slide-style recap is often coherent when each format has a defined job. What format is best for software training? Use authentic screen recording or simulation when interface detail matters, supported by stable diagrams or slides for durable concepts. Plan for software updates. What format is best for compliance training? There is no single best format. Use stable policy summaries, realistic decisions or scenarios, searchable source material, and assessment appropriate to the risk. Choose the evidence learners need The best training video format is the one that reveals the information needed for correct performance with the least unnecessary cognitive and maintenance burden. Animate meaningful change, stabilise material that needs inspection, and use authentic footage when fidelity matters. To prototype both explanatory and presentation-led approaches from existing material, start with Knowlify’s training video maker . Verify current style, input, export, accessibility, and plan capabilities before selecting a format for a full programme. title: The Complete Guide to Payments in Sierra Leone 2026: Virtual Cards, Mobile Money & Visa Fees
summary: Visiting Sierra Leone in 2026? Get visa-on-arrival fees, eVisa timelines, mobile money info, and the best virtual card for paying online abroad.
body_text: Most visitors to Sierra Leone need either a visa on arrival (around USD 80, issued at Lungi International Airport and land borders) or an pre-applied eVisa applied for in advance at (USD 80, roughly 3 business days to process). ECOWAS/African Union citizens often pay less or nothing. Cash still dominates day-to-day spending, but mobile money (Orange Money, Afrimoney) and internationally enabled virtual card providers like Miden are the easiest ways to pay online before and during your trip, from booking hotels to covering conference and MICE event fees. This guide covers everything you need to plan a 2026 trip to Sierra Leone: entry requirements, when to go, what to see, how to pay for things ( choosing the best virtual card provider for international payments ), business and event travel, safety, and answers to the questions people ask most. Banana Island - Sierra Leone 1. Why Visit Sierra Leone in 2026 Sierra Leone is one of West Africa's most underrated destinations. Palm-lined Atlantic beaches, the Freetown Peninsula's forested hills, chimpanzee sanctuaries, and a warm, fast-recovering tourism scene are just a few of the things that make this area memorable. Freetown is also becoming a regional hub for conferences, trade fairs, and NGO/government events, which means more travelers are arriving each year not just for the beaches, but for business. Whether you're coming for River Number 2 Beach, the Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary, or a multi-day MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions) event in Freetown, the big three; visas, money, and payments, are what every traveler needs to sort out first. This guide walks through each one. You Might Also Like: Top 10 places to visit in Sierra Leone 2. Entry Requirements: Visa on Arrival & eVisa in Sierra Leone Sierra Leone offers two main entry routes for tourists and business travelers; a visa on arrival at official ports of entry, and an eVisa applied for online before you fly. Whichever one applies to you depends on your nationality. On-Arrival Visa Sierra Leone: What to Know Available at Freetown International Airport (Lungi) and at land borders including Jendema (Liberia) and Gbalamuya (Guinea). Standard fee is roughly USD 80 for most eligible nationalities (some third-party facilitators quote higher all-in prices, so always check the official rate first). ECOWAS/African Union citizens often pay less — some nationalities are charged around USD 25, and a handful (e.g., Botswana, Eswatini, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritius) are issued a free visa on arrival under reciprocal agreements. Visas on arrival are typically valid for 30 days, single entry. You'll need: a passport valid 6+ months beyond your stay, proof of onward/return travel, accommodation details, and your yellow fever vaccination card (mandatory, checked on landing). eVisa Option Citizens of countries not eligible for visa-on-arrival must apply for an eVisa in advance through the official portal. Cost is around USD 80, with processing usually completed within a few business days. Apply only through the official government portal — third-party sites often charge extra "service fees" for the same visa. Check your Country’s Visa eligibility here: Sierra Leone Free Visa Eligible Countries Official Embassy Visa Fee Schedule (Washington, D.C.) If you're applying for a Sierra Leone visa in advance through an embassy or consulate rather than on arrival, the Embassy of Sierra Leone in Washington, D.C. publishes the following official fee schedule for visas processed there (fees payable by money order or cashier's check only — non-refundable): Visa Category Single Entry Multiple Entry Requirement Tourist / Visitor $100 $150 Up to 30 days per visit Business $100 $150 Letter from employer required Transit $30 N/A Max 72 hours, onward ticket required Student $75 $100 Enrollment letter required Journalist / Media $100 $150 Press credentials required Diplomatic / Official Gratis Gratis Diplomatic note required Expedited Service (add-on) +$50 +$50 2–3 business days Source: Embassy of Sierra Leone, Washington, D.C. Practical Tip: The embassy's pre-arrival fees ($100–$150) are noticeably higher than the ~$80 figure commonly quoted for the on-arrival visa at Lungi Airport. If your nationality is eligible for visa-on-arrival, applying at Lungi may be cheaper than going through an embassy; if it isn't, you'll need to go through an embassy or the eVisa portal instead. Always confirm the exact, current fee with your nearest Sierra Leone embassy/consulate or directly inside the evisa.sl application before booking your trip. Peninsula Beaches- Sierra Leone 3. Money, Payments & the Best Virtual Cards for Sierra Leone Sierra Leone remains a largely cash-based economy outside major hotels and businesses in Freetown. For anything you need to pay online before or during your trip — flights, hotels, visa fees, conference tickets — a virtual visa card for international payments is generally the fastest, safest option, especially if your home bank card gets blocked for "unusual" overseas or online activity. Local Currency & Cash The Official currency is the Sierra Leonean Leone (SLL). Carry cash (USD or EUR travel in clean, newer bills) for markets, local transport, and smaller restaurants. ATMs exist in Freetown but are not universally reliable outside the capital. Don't depend on them as your only source of funds. Mobile Money Mobile money is the backbone of everyday digital payments in Sierra Leone: Orange Money and Africell's Afrimoney are the two dominant providers, used for everything from utility bills to hotel and restaurant payments. Both now offer prepaid Visa cards linked to mobile money wallets, letting users without a traditional bank account make local and international online payments. A useful context if you're paying local vendors, staff, or partners while in-country. Setting up a local mobile money account as a short-term tourist is possible but usually requires a local SIM and ID, so it's more practical for longer stays, NGO staff, or business travelers than a one-week beach holiday. How to Choose the Best Virtual Card for Online Payments in Sierra Leone Because card acceptance is still uneven and international transfers to Sierra Leone can be slow or costly, many travelers, event organizers, and businesses use a virtual card to handle end-to-end travel logistics. When comparing the best virtual card for online payments in this context, look for: Global acceptance with Visa or Mastercard networks (important since local card infrastructure is still developing) Instant issuance so you're not waiting days before a trip or event deadline. Multi-currency support to avoid repeated conversion fees between USD, EUR, and SLE. Low or no cross-border fees, since you'll likely be paying vendors, hotels, or organizers based outside your home country. Spending controls — the ability to load a fixed amount, which is useful for managing event budgets or per-trip spending caps. Business Travel & MICE Events in Sierra Leone Freetown has increasingly hosted MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions) activity: government summits, NGO forums, trade expos, and regional business gatherings. title: How to Know You Have a Narcissistic Mother
summary: Wondering if your mom is narcissistic? Learn the signs of a narcissistic mother, how it impacts you, and how LunaJoy’s expert therapists can help you heal.
body_text: Do you often feel like your mother’s love comes with strings attached? Or that no matter what you do, it’s never quite enough? If you’re wondering whether your mom is narcissistic, you’re not alone. Many adult children grapple with the emotional scars left by narcissistic parenting. Recognizing the signs of a narcissistic mother is the first step toward understanding your experiences and starting the healing process. In this article, we’ll break down common narcissistic mother traits, how they show up in parenting, and what you can do to reclaim your emotional well-being. The good news? You don’t have to navigate this journey alone. At LunaJoy , we specialize in helping individuals heal from the impact of toxic family dynamics. Ready to learn more? Keep reading. What Is Narcissistic Personality Disorder (NPD)? Narcissistic Personality Disorder (NPD) is a mental health condition characterized by an inflated sense of self-importance, a deep need for constant attention, and a lack of empathy. People with NPD often struggle with fragile self-esteem and may exhibit manipulative behaviors to maintain their sense of superiority. When a parent exhibits narcissistic traits, it can profoundly affect their children. This dynamic—known as parental narcissism—often leads to emotional neglect, feelings of inadequacy, and lifelong challenges with healthy relationships. 15 Signs of a Narcissistic Mother Lack of Empathy A narcissistic mother struggles to understand or validate the emotions of others. She may dismiss your struggles or pain, claiming you're "too sensitive" or "making a big deal out of nothing." This lack of empathy can create a profound emotional disconnect, leaving you feeling invisible and unsupported. For example, if you’re grieving a loss or celebrating a major accomplishment, she might hijack the conversation or fail to acknowledge your feelings altogether. Over time, this emotional void can lead to feelings of loneliness and insecure attachment styles in adult relationships. Excessive Need for Control A narcissistic mother thrives on control. From dictating how you should dress or what career to pursue to interfering in your friendships and romantic relationships, her involvement may feel suffocating. This control often extends to subtle manipulation, like steering conversations to align with her agenda or using guilt to influence your decisions. Her need for control isn’t about love; it’s about maintaining power and ensuring her place as the authority figure in your life. Unrealistic Expectations A narcissistic mother often holds her children to impossibly high standards, expecting perfection in academics, appearance, or behavior. If you don’t meet these standards, you may face relentless criticism or punishment. These expectations may seem less about your success and more about her desire to look good to others. Over time, this creates a sense of inadequacy as you internalize the idea that you’re never good enough. For example, you may feel constant pressure to achieve higher grades, excel in extracurricular activities, or even live out the dreams she couldn’t fulfill herself. Emotional Manipulation and Gaslighting Emotional manipulation is a key tool in a narcissistic mother’s arsenal. She may twist your words, deny past events, or tell you, "That never happened," making you doubt your reality. This gaslighting tactic allows her to deflect blame and maintain control over the narrative. For example, if you confront her about hurtful behavior, she might respond with, “I can’t believe you’d accuse me of that. After everything I’ve done for you.” This leaves you questioning your perceptions and feelings, creating confusion and emotional turmoil. Playing the Victim A narcissistic mother often reframes conflicts to make herself the victim. If you set boundaries or address her harmful behavior, she may accuse you of being ungrateful, selfish, or even cruel. For example, if you express your need for space, she might respond with, “I guess I’m just a terrible mother, then.” This deflection serves to guilt you into compliance and shifts the focus away from her actions. Focusing on Appearance and Social Status For a narcissistic mother, appearances matter above all else. She may pressure you to conform to her idealized image of success, often prioritizing outward achievements over inner well-being. This could manifest as insisting you dress a certain way, excel in specific activities, or maintain friendships that enhance her social standing. Beneath this focus on appearances is often a deep-seated sense of inadequacy she’s projecting outward. Conditional Love and Approval Her love may feel like it has strings attached. When you meet her expectations, she showers you with praise and affection. However, the moment you fail to deliver, her warmth disappears. This conditional love teaches you that affection is earned, not freely given. For instance, she might show pride in your achievements only if they align with her vision for your life, leaving you feeling like your personal dreams or goals are irrelevant. Rivalry or Jealousy Toward the Child Instead of celebrating your successes, a narcissistic mother may see you as a competition. This rivalry could manifest in subtle ways, like offering backhanded compliments, or in more overt behaviors, such as undermining your achievements. For example, if you receive a promotion or praise, she might downplay it by saying, “Well, it’s not like you’re the CEO.” This jealousy often stems from her fragile self-esteem and fear of being overshadowed by her own child. Constant Criticism Living with a narcissistic mother often means enduring relentless criticism. She may nitpick your appearance, decisions, or achievements, framing her harsh words as “helpful advice.” Over time, this constant criticism can erode your self-confidence , making you doubt your worth and abilities. For instance, if you try something new, she might say, “Why would you do that? You’re just setting yourself up for failure,” rather than offering encouragement or support. Sensitivity to Criticism While she freely criticizes others, a narcissistic mother often reacts poorly to even the mildest feedback. Her responses may range from anger to tears, often making the situation about her feelings rather than addressing the issue at hand. For example, if you calmly point out how her behavior hurt you, she might respond with, “I guess I’m just a terrible person,” turning the focus away from her actions and onto her emotions. Emotional Neglect Growing up with a narcissist mother often means your emotional needs were not met. She might have been physically present but emotionally unavailable, leaving you feeling unseen and unheard. This neglect can lead to a lasting sense of emptiness and difficulty trusting others. For example, if you needed comfort after a tough day, she might have dismissed you with, “You’re fine, stop overreacting,” rather than offering support or validation. Need to Be the Center of Attention In any situation, a narcissistic mother will find a way to redirect the spotlight onto herself. Whether it’s a family gathering, your wedding, or even your birthday, she might create drama or steer conversations to keep herself as the focal point. For instance, she might tell a story about her struggles during your graduation party, overshadowing your accomplishments. Using Guilt as a Weapon A narcissistic mother is a master at using guilt to control her children. She might say things like, “I sacrificed so much for you, and this is the thanks I get?” or “If you don’t visit me, I’ll just be all alone.” These guilt trips are designed to make you feel responsible for her happiness, prioritizing her needs over your own. Dismissal of Your Achievements No matter how significant your accomplishments, a narcissistic mother might find ways to diminish them. She could say, “That’s nice, but what about…” or compare your success to someone else’s. This dismissal isn’t accidental—it’s a tactic to ensure the focus remains on her. For instance, if you earn a promotion, she might respond with, “That’s great, but remember, I worked two jobs at your age.” Lack of Boundaries A narcissistic mother often disregards personal boundaries, treating your life as an extension of hers. She might invade your privacy, pry into your personal relationships, or offer unsolicited advice about your parenting. For example, she might show up unannounced at your home or insist on being included in decisions that don’t concern her. This lack of boundaries creates a sense of powerlessness, as it feels impossible to carve out space for yourself. Why It’s Hard to Recognize When Your Mom Is Narcissistic Growing up in a narcissistic family, you may not realize that the dynamics are unhealthy. These behaviors can feel normal, especially if you’ve never seen a healthier alternative. The society also complicates recognition. Mothers are often idealized as selfless and nurturing, making it difficult to reconcile the idea of a narcissistic mother with societal expectations. Many children of narcissistic parents internalize the blame. You might think, “Maybe I’m too sensitive,” or, “I’m just not good enough.” This conditioning keeps you stuck in a cycle of doubt, making it harder to see the reality of maternal narcissism. How to Cope with a Narcissistic Mother Recognize the Problem The first step in coping is acknowledging that your mom is narcissistic and understanding how her behaviors have affected you. This awareness allows you to stop blaming yourself for the relationship's toxicity and start focusing on your healing. Recognizing patterns like emotional manipulation or constant criticism can help you see the root cause of your struggles. Remember, her behavior stems from her issues, not your worth. Set Healthy Boundaries Boundaries are crucial for protecting yourself from emotional harm. Decide what behaviors you’re willing to tolerate and communicate your limits clearly. For instance, you might limit discussions about personal matters or request she stop criticizing your choices. Boundaries are about creating space for your well-being, not about punishing her. Stay consistent even if she reacts negatively—it’s a sign your boundaries are working. Seek Professional Support Therapy can be a lifeline when dealing with the effects of narcissistic parenting. A skilled therapist can help you process emotions, navigate difficult conversations, and rebuild your self-esteem. Therapy also provides tools for managing guilt and conflict, which often accompany efforts to change the dynamics with a narcissistic mother. Limit Contact (If Necessary) Sometimes, limiting or cutting contact is necessary for your peace of mind. This doesn’t mean you don’t care about your mother; it means prioritizing your emotional health. If you choose this route, explain your decision calmly and stick to it, even if she tries to guilt you into reconnecting. Focus on Your Healing Healing isn’t just about coping with your mother’s behavior—it’s about reclaiming your sense of self. Engage in self-care practices that nourish your mind and body, such as journaling, mindfulness, or spending time with supportive people. Surrounding yourself with individuals who respect and uplift you is key to building the healthy relationships you deserve. Helping you rebuild your self-worth and confidence. Guiding you toward fulfilling, healthy relationships free from toxicity. Take the first step toward emotional freedom. title: Growing back a forest: AirHelp's “Plant a Tree” program, supporting projects in Portugal and beyond
summary: AirHelp pledges a tree for every 100 flight delays worldwide. See how that's helping restore Portugal's Leiria forest and five other projects.
body_text: Some of the flights we help protect with AirHelp+ membership fly directly over the Leiria Pine Forest, a stretch of woodland on Portugal's Atlantic coast that's been part of the landscape for more than 700 years. In 2017, most of it burned down in a single day. Through our Plant a Tree program, we've been supporting the effort to bring it back — and Leiria is just one of numerous projects we currently support around the world. A forest with 700 years of history — gone in 24 hours The Leiria Pine Forest was first planted in the thirteenth century, ordered by a Portuguese king to stop coastal dunes and wind-blown sand from swallowing nearby farmland. Over the centuries it grew into more than 11,000 hectares of woodland — a source of timber for Portugal's famous Age of Discovery ships, and a place generations of local families still walk, picnic, and swim near today. In October 2017, a wildfire driven by strong winds and drought tore through 86% of the forest in a single day. Only a fraction of the original woodland survived. The replanting effort Since 2022, the nonprofit One Tree Planted and its local partners have been restoring the forest, planting over a million native, fire-resilient trees across nearly 1,000 hectares. The goal isn't just to replace what burned — it's to bring back a more resilient mix of species than existed before, so the forest stands a better chance against future fires. That means native trees and shrubs that stabilize the coastal dunes and sandy soil, support local wildlife, and rebuild the forest's natural firebreaks, alongside the maritime pines that made the area famous. Local schools and residents have taken part directly, growing saplings in nearby nurseries and helping plant them by hand. Why it matters As passenger rights advocates, caring about people who fly means caring about the places they fly over and through — which is the reasoning behind AirHelp’s tree planting program. Three things drive it specifically: Restoring nature and biodiversity: the projects the program supports create new habitats and protect biodiversity, and trees clean air and water while supporting a healthy climate. Giving back to the places we fly over: flight disruptions create up to 9 million tons of CO2 every year worldwide, and the average tree absorbs an average of 10 kilograms, or 22 pounds, of carbon dioxide per year for the first 20 years — a direct, if partial, counterweight. Supporting local communities: green spaces support the health and wellbeing of the people who live near them, and agroforestry projects boost local economies and reduce food insecurity. The pledge and the numbers The program runs on a simple pledge: AirHelp plants one tree for every 100 flight delays it tracks worldwide, turning a bad flight into something good for the planet. As of writing, that pledge has added up to 228,833 trees planted, tracked against 22,883,328 delayed flights — figures that update continuously as more flights are tracked, so check the live counter for the current total. There's a natural overlap worth naming here: the same disruption tracking that feeds this pledge is what AirHelp uses to check whether a delayed or cancelled flight owes you compensation. If your own flight has been delayed recently, it's already part of the data behind these numbers — and it's worth a quick check in the AirHelp app to see whether it also owes you something more directly, like up to €600 compensation. Stress-free flying is a download away Get instant flight alerts, see your rights in real time, and claim compensation in minutes. Download our app Loved by 1 million travellers and counting available for: Where else we're planting Portugal is one of the most detailed stories so far, but AirHelp’s tree planting program currently supports reforestation projects in multiple countries and continents, each addressing a different kind of land degradation. Here are some examples: Armenia — North Bazum reforestation: restoring land degraded by intensive animal grazing, planting native trees and shrubs to reduce bare ground and rebuild a stronger ecosystem. Spain — regenerative agriculture: food trees are planted across farms and public land, mitigating desertification while creating habitat for lynx, foxes, and other wildlife. Nova Scotia, Canada — Cape Breton Highlands restoration: replanting native spruce after decades of moose grazing prevented natural regrowth following a spruce budworm outbreak. Germany — climate-resilient restoration: volunteers and landowners rebuilding forests damaged by drought, storms, and bark beetle infestation with more pest-resistant, mixed-species planting. Turkey — agroforestry farming: distributing olive and pistachio seedlings to farmers in regions affected by desertification, boosting local income alongside land recovery. Each project is implemented by One Tree Planted's local partners on the ground, chosen because the type of restoration needed — dune stabilization, agroforestry, pest-resistant replanting — differs from place to place. What it means for travelers You don't need to do anything to be part of this — it's simply something AirHelp chose to support through our Plant a Tree program . But if you're flying through Portugal, Spain, Germany, Turkey, Armenia, or eastern Canada, it's worth knowing that the landscape you might glimpse from the window could be part of one of these six projects. Read more about what drives us on our about us page. You can read the full story of the Leiria restoration project on One Tree Planted's site. title: Legora announces major New York City expansion
summary: Nearly 100,000-square-foot Manhattan office will anchor Legora's North American growth, supporting engineering, product and legal engineering teams.
body_text: Legora, the agentic operating system for legal work, today announced a major expansion of its US operations with a new office at 11 Madison Avenue in Manhattan. The move will create over 550 new jobs and establish nearly 100,000 square feet of office space supporting engineering, product development, legal engineering and corporate functions. The expansion is backed by New York State's Empire State Development, which has offered up to $10.5 million through the Excelsior Jobs Program in support of Legora's investment and job creation commitments. “Artificial intelligence is reshaping industries around the world, and New York is making sure we remain at the forefront of that transformation,” New York Governor Kathy Hochul said. “Legora’s decision to grow its U.S. operations in New York City is another vote of confidence in our unmatched talent, world-class innovation ecosystem and commitment to helping cutting-edge companies succeed. By investing in companies creating the technologies of tomorrow, we’re creating the good-paying jobs that will drive New York’s economy for years to come.” CRO of Legora Patrick Forquer said: "New York is establishing itself as the epicentre of legal AI, and we intend to be part of that story. This office anchors our North American growth, and we're building it alongside a world-class team and customers who are shaping the future of legal work." CFO of Legora David Eckstein said: "With more than 1,500 law firm and corporate customers across 50 markets globally, this office will allow us to expand our presence and provide best-in-class support to our growing customer base." The 98,420-square-foot office will support a broad range of functions, including engineering, legal engineering, product development and corporate operations, as Legora builds out its New York presence over the coming years. Empire State Development President, CEO and Commissioner Hope Knight said: "Every major AI company that chooses to grow in New York strengthens an ecosystem that is becoming more competitive with each new investment. Legora's expansion will create opportunities for New Yorkers, accelerate innovation and reinforce the momentum we're seeing as global technology companies continue to put down deeper roots across the state." Legora's expansion is supported by Governor Hochul's strategy to position New York as a premier destination for artificial intelligence, fintech and other high-growth technology companies. In recent years, companies across the AI ecosystem have continued to expand their presence in the state, drawn by its workforce, access to capital, universities and innovation environment.

In the second quarter, Aerospace Technologies segment sales of $4.5 billion grew 5% organically year over year. Mechanical supply chain showed sequential improvement during the quarter though material supply continued to limit sales growth across end markets. Sales growth was led by a 17% increase in Commercial aviation original equipment due to shipments recoupling to build schedules, particularly in commercial air transport, and a 7% increase in Commercial aviation aftermarket driven by increasing demand from the installed base. Defense and space sales were flat as continued strong demand was constrained by output and program timing. Segment profit grew 2% from the prior year to $1.1 billion, which included approximately $40 million of inventory obsolescence charges related to lower demand for pockets of existing inventory stock driven by emerging repair technologies extending product lives. of certain non-GAAP financial measures presented in this press release to which reconciliations are attached to the most directly comparable financial measures calculated and presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP). The reconciliations include the financial measures on a consolidated Honeywell basis and include adjustments related to the separation of Honeywell Aerospace (the Separation Adjustments). The amounts shown as Separation Adjustments are unaudited and represent our best estimates. Management believes that, when considered together with reported amounts, these measures are useful to investors and management in understanding our ongoing operations and in the analysis of ongoing operating trends. These measures should be considered in addition to, and not as replacements for, the most comparable GAAP measure. Certain measures presented on a non-GAAP basis represent the impact of adjusting items net of tax. The tax-effect for adjusting items is determined individually and on a case-by-case basis. Other companies may calculate these non-GAAP measures differently, limiting the usefulness of these measures for comparative purposes. Management does not consider these non-GAAP measures in isolation or as an alternative to financial measures determined in accordance with GAAP. The principal limitations of these non-GAAP financial measures are that they exclude significant expenses and income that are required by GAAP to be recognized in the consolidated financial statements. In addition, they are subject to inherent limitations as they reflect the exercise of judgments by management about which expenses and income are excluded or included in determining these non-GAAP financial measures. Investors are urged to review the reconciliation of the non-GAAP financial measures to the comparable GAAP financial measures and not to rely on any single financial measure to evaluate Honeywell's and Honeywell Technologies’ businesses. As indicated herein, certain forward-looking non-GAAP financial measures are not reconciled because management cannot reliably predict or estimate certain items for the reasons specified herein with respect to each non-GAAP financial measure.
